messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's canary -> prod for lightning-18b-qlora embeddings, semantic-search median cosine on our v2 benchmark dropped ~5-8% vs baseline. Not huge but consistent across two datasets.

jake: Ugh. Was quantization applied differently than the eval harness?

maria: Canary used 4-bit NFQ quant; prod used the same bits but with different kernel (fusedq on A100). I double-checked the config: `quant_profile: nfq-4` but runtime picks `fusedq` kernel at serve-time.

sasha: Any tokenizer drift? New model release bumped tokenizer config?

maria: Tokenizer appears identical — same vocab + merges. I ran a token-level diff on 10k samples, <0.2% divergence. So unlikely tokenizer.

maria: Quick repro steps I ran locally:
```python
from redwood_client import EmbeddingClient
client = EmbeddingClient(model='lightning-18b-qlora', quant='nfq-4')
base = client.embed(batch_A)  # baseline snapshots from previous release
new = client.embed(batch_A)  # current prod instance
# compute median cosine drop
```
I can paste full script if helpful.

jake: Can you attach a tiny histogram or a couple of example pairs where similarity dropped a lot?

maria: Attached inline numbers: median_cosine_baseline=0.82, median_cosine_prod=0.76. Top 3 large drops: pair ids [421, 1902, 8877] dropped 0.18, 0.14, 0.12 respectively.

ci-bot: Deployment record: `deploy/embeddings/lightning-18b-qlora` -> succeeded by @deploy-bot at 2348597000. Canary duration 3h, traffic cutover 2348598000.

sasha: Hypotheses: 1) fusedq kernel subtly changes float accumulation leading to small direction shifts. 2) KV cache truncation? But embeddings shouldn't use KV. 3) Serving pre/post-normalization difference (L2 norm vs none).

maria: Good call on normalization — our eval harness expects L2-normalized vectors. Prod was normalizing in the client layer, but the runtime started normalizing again after an optimization change, so we may be double-normalizing in some paths.

jake: If double-normalization happened, cosine shouldn't change (because normalized twice still unit norm) — unless there was a numerical precision bug during fused kernel output. Could be re-normalizing on quantized outputs causing scale shifts.

maria: Agree. I ran this quick check: unnormalized dot products match within 1e-3, but after normalization prod values shift more. So likely numerical edge-case in fusedq post-processing.

sasha: Next steps:
- maria: run micro-repro on A100 fusedq vs non-fused kernel (owner: maria, ETA: 3h)
- jake: add additional regression test to CI that computes median cosine over small seed and fails if drop >3% (owner: jake, ETA: EOD)
- sasha: roll a quick canary rollback to kernel=standard on 10% traffic if we confirm (owner: sasha, ETA: after maria confirms)

maria: Starting micro-repro now. Will include a deterministic seed and code to pin kernels: `REDWOOD_KERNEL=standard` vs `REDWOOD_KERNEL=fusedq`.

jake: For the CI test, keep it light (100 queries) and run on the quantized path. We don't want CI flakiness. Also add an env flag to skip on hardware that can't reproduce fusedq.

maria: Update: micro-repro completed locally on A100 instance — fusedq median=0.758, standard median=0.819. Same delta as prod. Saving logs to s3://redwood-debug/lightning18b/2348600000/ (I'll post link).

sasha: OK let's do a controlled rollback to `kernel=standard` on the embeddings fleet for site-prod. I'll open a rollout with canary 5% and monitor embedding median.

ci-bot: Rollout plan created: `rollback-kernel-standard` by @sasha, canary=5%, start at 2348600300. Monitor: embeddings-median-cosine, p50 latency, token-cost.

maria: I've also opened an issue in GitHub: redwood-inference/runtime#4123 with diffs and numeric traces. Putting the micro-repro script in the issue.

jake: After rollback, we should add a unit test to fusedq that compares outputs vs standard for a numeric set (tolerances adjusted for quant). If fusedq can't meet tolerance, we should gate it behind a flag.

sasha: Agree. Also add canary alert: if median drops >2% during rollout, auto-rollback.

maria: Thanks team. I'll paste the S3 link and PR IDs here once available. :thumbsup:

jake: Thanks — lemme know if you want infra help spinning repro A100s. :handshake:

sasha: Nice catch, maria. Good triage. :eyes:
